title: mathAgents G-CX counterexample log
description: reports/dossiers/<slug>/counterexamples.json. Stage 6 counterexample candidates and the human G-CX verdicts on them, keyed to each target declaration's statement_fingerprint from reports/kernel/latest.json (spec DD-15, DD-16, DD-39). Agents log candidates; no agent writes a verdict approval (DD-29). A waiver records an operator kernel-as-judge override for one conversation (D5, D26); a waived refutation needs a kernel-proved Lean witness and yields the label 'refuted, verdict-waived' (DD-59).

lean_namespace.description: Lean namespace holding this dossier's declarations; every target and witness must lie under it.

decl.description: Fully-qualified Lean name of the statement the candidate targets.

statement_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the target statement when the candidate was logged. A later change means the statement was revised after this counterexample.

engine.description: Engine id from references/prover-engines.json, when an engine found it.

lean_witness.description: Fully-qualified Lean theorem re-establishing the counterexample, written `theorem cx_<n> : ¬ (type_of% @<target>)` under `<lean_namespace>.CX` (or, for a target revised since logging, with the logged statement written out in full); its kernel-report negates_fingerprint must equal this entry's statement_fingerprint. Required for decide/smt/atp refutations (DD-16) and for waived refutes or revise verdicts (DD-59). Recorded only by `scripts/log_counterexample.py witness`.

toolchain_pin.description: The instance's lean/lean-toolchain when this was recorded (docs/lean-version-governance.md R6). Optional; stamped by `log_counterexample.py add`. Not compared with the current pin: the log is append-only, so an entry keeps the pin it was logged under.

mathlib_rev.description: The Mathlib commit (lake-manifest.json rev) when this was recorded (R6). Optional; stamped and kept like toolchain_pin.

decision.description: refutes: the statement is false; spurious: the candidate does not refute it; revise: the counterexample is accepted and the statement was revised.

statement_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the statement as it stands when the verdict is given; for 'revise', the revised statement's fingerprint.
